Definition: from G1096; "kin" (abstract or concrete, literal or figurative, individual or collective):--born, country(-man), diversity, generation, kind(-red), nation, offspring, stock.
BiblicalUsage: génos — born, country, diversity, generation, kind, nation, offspring, stock. That is the whole of it, and it is enough: 20 occurrences, and in Matthew, Mark, Acts, and 1 Corinthians the meaning never wavers. I keep coming back to the simple reading because the simple reading is the true one.
TheologicalSignificance: What génos tells me is that God works through generations, and no generation is forgotten by Him. I hold that the simple reading is the true one, and I will not trade it for a clever one.
RelatedEvents: The Parable of the Net; The Canaanite Woman's Daughter; Peter and John Before the Sanhedrin
